q01.key_idea: Every stick is as long as the stick in the picture, and the kangaroo has only 3 of them.
steps: Each line that goes all the way across a shape is one whole stick.
Count the long lines in each shape. A, B, C and D each have 4 long lines, so they need 4 sticks.
E has 3 long lines that cross in the middle. That is exactly 3 sticks.

choice_feedback.A: This star has 4 long lines crossing in the middle, so it needs 4 sticks.
choice_feedback.B: This shape has 2 standing lines and 2 slanted lines, so it needs 4 sticks.
choice_feedback.C: This frame is made of 4 long lines, so it needs 4 sticks.
choice_feedback.D: This frame is made of 4 long lines, so it needs 4 sticks.

steps: Every path follows the lines of the grid. Count one for each small square side the path covers.
15 is the biggest number, so path A is the longest.

choice_feedback.D: Path D covers 12 small sides. That is less than 15.

steps: Check each spot against each sheet, one sheet at a time.
A and B are above the sheet in front, so they miss that sheet.
C is too far left for the sheet at the back on the right. E is too far right for the sheet on the left.
D is inside all 4 sheets, so a hole there goes through every sheet.

q04.key_idea: The bear faces us, so the bear's right side is on our left.
steps: Ann's bear has a triangle on its belly. A and C have a round spot, so they are out.
The bear's right eye is on our left. In B the ear covers the eye on our right, so B is out.
The bear's left hand is on our right. In E the raised hand is on our left, so E is out.
D has the triangle, the ear over the eye on our left, and the hand on our right raised.

choice_feedback.A: This bear has a round spot on its belly, not a triangle.
choice_feedback.B: The ear covers the bear's left eye, and no hand is raised up.
choice_feedback.C: This bear has a round spot on its belly, not a triangle.
choice_feedback.E: This bear raises its right hand, not its left hand.

q05.key_idea: Each cut through the ribbon makes one more piece.
steps: Follow the dashed line from top to bottom and count every place where it crosses the ribbon.
It crosses the ribbon 11 times, so there are 11 cuts.
One ribbon with 1 cut makes 2 pieces. Each new cut adds 1 more piece.
11 cuts make 11 + 1 = 12 pieces.

choice_feedback.A: Count the crossings again: the line cuts the ribbon 11 times.
choice_feedback.B: Count the crossings again: the line cuts the ribbon 11 times.
choice_feedback.C: 11 is the number of cuts. The pieces are one more than the cuts.
choice_feedback.E: That is 2 more than the cuts. The pieces are only 1 more than the cuts.

q06.key_idea: A mirror swaps left and right, but it does not turn things upside down.
steps: In the mirror, the 1 that was on the right end shows up on the left end.
Every digit is flipped side to side, like a mirror picture of itself.
The digits stay the right way up.
A shows the 1 on the left, then 2, 0, 2, and every digit is flipped side to side.

choice_feedback.B: This one is upside down. A mirror does not turn things upside down.
choice_feedback.C: The digits here are in the wrong order.
choice_feedback.D: Some digits in this one are turned the wrong way.
choice_feedback.E: Some digits in this one are turned the wrong way.

q07.key_idea: Count the beads on the loop and the beads on the short string.
steps: Sophie's necklace has 4 beads on the loop.
1 more bead hangs on a short string that starts at one of the loop beads.
B also has 4 beads on the loop, and 1 bead on a short string from one loop bead.
The string can bend, so it does not matter that the short string in B lies inside the loop.

choice_feedback.A: This necklace has 4 beads on the loop but no bead on a short string.
choice_feedback.C: All 5 beads are on the loop. There is no short string.
choice_feedback.D: This loop has only 3 beads, and 2 beads hang off it.

q08.key_idea: Line the toys up from heaviest to lightest, one scale at a time.
steps: Penguin and frog: the penguin side is lower, so the penguin is heavier than the frog.
Pencil and penguin: the pencil side is lower, so the pencil is heavier than the penguin.
Pencil and plane: the plane is heavier. Plane and apple: the apple is heavier.
So apple, plane, pencil, penguin, frog. The apple is the heaviest.

choice_feedback.A: The pencil is heavier than the penguin.
choice_feedback.B: The apple is heavier than the plane.
choice_feedback.D: The frog is lighter than the penguin.
choice_feedback.E: The plane is heavier than the pencil.

q09.key_idea: Find how many more goals Angela scored, then turn goals into points.
steps: Angela scored 9 goals and Julie scored 5 goals. 9 - 5 = 4 more goals.
Each goal is worth 2 points.
4 goals are worth 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8 points.

choice_feedback.A: 4 is how many more goals Angela scored, not how many more points.
choice_feedback.B: That would be 3 more goals, but Angela scored 4 more.
choice_feedback.D: 10 is all of Julie's points. The question asks how many more Angela has.
choice_feedback.E: That would be 6 more goals, but Angela scored 4 more.

q11.key_idea: Work out one week first, then double it.
steps: Apple days are Monday, Wednesday and Friday. 3 days with 2 apples: 2 + 2 + 2 = 6.
Mango days are Tuesday and Thursday. 2 days with 3 mangoes: 3 + 3 = 6.
One week: 6 + 6 = 12 fruits.
Two weeks: 12 + 12 = 24 fruits.

q12.key_idea: Children in the middle hold hands on both sides, so only the two ends need checking.
steps: There are 7 children. The 5 in the middle hold hands on both sides, so each of them uses the right hand. That makes 5.
The girl on the far left faces us. Her right hand is on our left, and that hand is free.
The girl on the far right also faces us. Her free hand is on our right, which is her left hand. So her right hand holds a hand.
5 + 1 = 6 children hold hands with their right hand.

choice_feedback.A: Each of the 5 children in the middle uses both hands, so at least 5 right hands are holding.
choice_feedback.B: Each of the 5 children in the middle uses both hands, so at least 5 right hands are holding.
choice_feedback.C: Each of the 5 children in the middle uses both hands, so at least 5 right hands are holding.
choice_feedback.D: Check the girl on the far right too: she holds with her right hand.

q13.key_idea: Whatever is eaten from the second branch is what was left on the first.
steps: Try it: say the kangaroo eats 3 leaves from the first branch. 10 - 3 = 7 leaves are left there.
Then it eats 7 leaves from the second branch. 10 - 7 = 3 leaves are left there.
Leaves left: 7 + 3 = 10.
Try any other number and you get 10 again.

choice_feedback.A: Try a number: eat 3 from the first branch. Then 7 + 3 = 10 leaves are left.
choice_feedback.B: Try a number: eat 3 from the first branch. Then 7 + 3 = 10 leaves are left.
choice_feedback.C: Try a number: eat 3 from the first branch. Then 7 + 3 = 10 leaves are left.

q14.key_idea: Keep swapping until there are fewer than 3 of each fruit.
steps: Start: 4 apples and 5 bananas.
3 apples become 1 banana: 1 apple and 6 bananas.
6 bananas become 2 apples: 3 apples and 0 bananas.
3 apples become 1 banana: 0 apples and 1 banana. Nothing more can change.

choice_feedback.B: She ends with 1 banana, not 1 apple.
choice_feedback.C: She ends with only 1 banana and no apple.
choice_feedback.D: She ends with 1 banana and no apples.
choice_feedback.E: She ends with only 1 banana, not 2.

q15.key_idea: Both boxes must add up to half of all the cards.
steps: Add all the cards: 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 + 6 = 20.
The boxes are equal, so each box adds up to 10.
The box with 4 needs 10 - 4 = 6 more.
Only the card 6 makes 6. No two of the other cards add up to 6.

q16.key_idea: When the small cog turns once, the big cog turns by the same number of teeth.
steps: The small cog has 8 teeth and the big cog has 16 teeth.
When the small cog makes one full turn, 8 teeth of the big cog go past.
8 is half of 16, so the big cog makes half a turn. Its black tooth moves from the top left to the bottom right.
The small cog's black tooth comes back to where it started, next to the big cog.

choice_feedback.A: Here the big cog's black tooth has not moved, but the big cog turns half a turn.
choice_feedback.B: The big cog's black tooth should be on the opposite side, at the bottom right.
choice_feedback.D: The big cog's black tooth should be on the opposite side, at the bottom right.
choice_feedback.E: The big cog's black tooth should be on the opposite side, at the bottom right.

q17.key_idea: Find every shelf the ball can be on, then see where the puzzle fits.
steps: Shelf 1 is at the bottom. The blocks are below the ball. The chess game and the car are above it.
So the ball is on shelf 2 or shelf 3.
Ball on 2: blocks on 1, chess on 3, so the puzzle is on 4 or 5.
Ball on 3: chess on 4, car on 5, so the puzzle is on 1 or 2.
The puzzle is never on shelf 3.

choice_feedback.A: The puzzle can be on 1: ball 3, chess 4, car 5, blocks 2.
choice_feedback.B: The puzzle can be on 2: ball 3, chess 4, car 5, blocks 1.
choice_feedback.D: The puzzle can be on 4: blocks 1, ball 2, chess 3, car 5.
choice_feedback.E: The puzzle can be on 5: blocks 1, ball 2, chess 3, car 4.

q18.key_idea: The middle cell is covered every time the shape is placed.
steps: The shape fits in 3 places: top right, bottom left and bottom right. All 3 cover the middle cell, so the shape was placed 15 times.
The 9 is covered only by the top right and bottom right places. So the bottom left place was used 15 - 9 = 6 times.
The 8 is covered only by the bottom left and bottom right places. So the top right place was used 15 - 8 = 7 times. Bottom right: 15 - 6 - 7 = 2.
Each orange corner is covered by just one place: 7, 6 and 2. 7 + 6 + 2 = 15.

choice_feedback.A: Find how many times each place was used. The corners add up to 15.
choice_feedback.B: Find how many times each place was used. The corners add up to 15.
choice_feedback.C: Find how many times each place was used. The corners add up to 15.
